questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a basic family need rather than a family want?
options: A brand new luxury sports car
A family vacation to another country
Nutritious daily meals
Designer wristwatches
questions.explain: Nutritious daily meals are essential for physical survival and health, making them a basic need. The others are wants or luxuries.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: How do 'family wants' differ from 'family needs'?
options: Wants are required for survival, while needs are not.
Needs are essential for survival, whereas wants are desires that are not strictly necessary.
Wants and needs have exactly the same meaning in family resource management.
Needs change every day, but wants remain permanent over a lifetime.
questions.explain: Needs are essential requirements for living (e.g., housing, food), whereas wants are things families desire to improve their lifestyle but can live without.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: What is the meaning of a 'family goal'?
options: An object or aim that the family works together to achieve within a timeframe.
The daily arguments among family members.
The minimum wage a family breadwinner earns.
An unnecessary item purchased on impulse.
questions.explain: A family goal is a specific target or objective, such as saving for a child's education or buying a house, that the family plans and works towards.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Paying the monthly utility bills (like electricity) is considered an example of a:
options: Long-term family goal
Short-term family goal
Psychological family need
Family value
questions.explain: Utility bills are recurring monthly expenses, making their payment a short-term goal compared to long-term goals like building a house.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: In Home Economics, 'family standards' are defined as:
options: The amount of taxes the family pays to the state.
The total number of children in a household.
The accepted level of quality, values, or behavior maintained by a family.
The physical size and location of the family's house.
questions.explain: Standards are the measures of quality or acceptable norms that a family adopts to evaluate their goals, behaviors, and way of living.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: What is the relationship between family needs, goals, and standards in resource management?
options: They contradict each other and make management impossible.
Needs create goals, and standards dictate the quality expected when achieving those goals.
Goals replace needs so standards are no longer required.
They have no connection with how a family utilizes its resources.
questions.explain: A family identifies its needs, which motivates them to set goals to fulfill those needs. The standards they hold determine the level of satisfaction required to achieve those goals.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: How do clear family goals assist in resource management?
options: They help prioritize spending and prevent waste of time and money.
They encourage families to borrow excessively from banks.
They force families to abandon their basic needs.
They decrease the available natural resources in the community.
questions.explain: Having clear goals provides a direction for the family's resources (like money and time), ensuring that they are allocated to what is most important and minimizing waste.
